title: iLTM: Integrated Large Tabular Model

problem.claim: Tabular data supports decisions across science, industry, and public services, but deep-learning advances have not fully transferred to tabular learning.

gap.claim: GBDTs remain a default practical choice, indicating a gap between tree-based methods and neural methods for tabular learning.

contributions.claim: iLTM is an integrated Large Tabular Model combining tree-derived embeddings, dimensionality-agnostic representations, a meta-trained hypernetwork, MLPs, and retrieval.
The model is pre-trained on more than 1,800 heterogeneous classification datasets.
iLTM is presented as a framework for tabular foundation models intended to bridge tree-based and neural methods.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize iLTM as a new framework for tabular foundation models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistently superior performance across tabular classification and regression tasks ranging from small datasets to large and high-dimensional tasks.
The authors report that, after light fine-tuning, the meta-trained hypernetwork transfers to regression targets and matches or surpasses strong baselines.
The authors report that extensive experiments outperform well-tuned GBDTs and leading deep tabular models while requiring less task-specific tuning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Tabular data is important across multiple decision-making domains.
Deep-learning progress has not fully carried over to tabular data, where GBDTs remain widely used.
iLTM integrates tree-derived and neural components with retrieval in one architecture.
The authors report broad performance advantages, transfer to regression, and reduced task-specific tuning.
The model is positioned as a new framework for robust, adaptable, and scalable tabular foundation models.

source_observation.claim: The architecture combines tree-derived embeddings, dimensionality-agnostic representations, a meta-trained hypernetwork, MLPs, and retrieval.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary tree-based and neural components may help address heterogeneous tabular tasks.

application.claim: For tabular foundation-model design, consider integrating inductive biases from tree methods with neural representations and retrieval.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which dataset characteristics or task conditions limit the reported advantages.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset-level performance values, evaluation metrics, or task-by-task comparisons.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, model scale, computational cost, or retrieval mechanism.
The abstract does not identify conditions under which iLTM may underperform.
